s009B1A.name: Game mode 09: erase file menu
summary: Game mode 09. Draws the ERASE DATA screen on top of the file select. The cursor chooses files (marking them in [$0DDE], bit 2 = file 0,
bit 0 = file 2) or END. On END, all marked files are cleared from both SRAM copies. Y or X cancels back to file select.
$009B80: long-call wrapper (called from the overworld in bank $04) that runs the CONTINUE/END menu for state [$13C9] - 1.

Ptrs009B8D.name: Pointer table: Continue/End menu, save prompt
summary: $009B8D: pointers for [$13C9] = 1 (draw CONTINUE/END) and 2 (run the menu: CONTINUE resets lives, END returns to the title).
$009BA8: wrapper for the overworld save prompt; entry 0 saves the game with the jingle ($1DF9 = 5), then closes the prompt.
$009BC9: save game routine. Copies $8D bytes from $1F49 to the file's SRAM slot at $70:xxxx plus a 16-bit checksum ($5A5A - sum),
and writes the same to the backup copy $1AD bytes later. Parameters: [$010A] = file number.
$009C13: closes the message box ([$1B87]++, [$1B88]++) and clears the stripe buffer with image $1B.

Instr009C1B.name: Tail of CODE_009C13 (JSR $9D29)
summary: These bytes are the opcodes for JSR $9D29 (show stripe image Y) listed as data; the RTL after them returns from CODE_009C13.

IntroControlData.name: Title demo: first buttons byte
summary: Buttons for demo segment 0 (Y + Right); the segment's duration is in ItrCntrlrSqnc.

ItrCntrlrSqnc.name: Title screen demo input script
summary: Recorded controller input for the title screen demo (Mario plays the intro level by himself). Buttons and times alternate: the first
buttons byte is at $009C1F, then time, buttons, time, ... Buttons use the format of [$15] (B Y Select Start Up Down Left Right).
$FF as buttons ends the demo.

GAMEMODE_07.name: Game mode 07: title screen and demo
summary: Runs the title screen. A press of B, Y, Select, Start, A or X (CODE_009CBE) leaves for the file select (game mode 08).
Otherwise the scripted input from ItrCntrlrSqnc is fed to the controller mirrors and the level engine runs the demo.
When the script ends the game mode is set to 2 and the title screen restarts. $009C89 is shared as 'go to game mode 2'.
$009CBE: Returns: Z = clear if no button is pressed.

s009CCB.name: Table: SRAM offsets of save files
summary: High and low bytes of the SRAM offset of each of the 3 save files ($0000, $008F, $011E; $8F bytes each). The backup copy is $1AD bytes after.

s009CD1.name: Game mode 08: file select, mode 0A: players
summary: $009CD1: file select (game mode 08). Selecting ERASE DATA goes to game mode 09. Selecting a file checks its checksum, repairs the
other copy from the good one, loads the file into $1F49-$1FD5 and goes to the player select (game mode 0A).
$009D38: copies the file menu tilemap into the stripe buffer and prints each file's exit count. $009DB5: verifies a file's checksum
(sum of $8D bytes + stored word = $5A5A) with fallback to the backup copy; returns Z set when valid, X = offset of the valid copy.
$009DFA: game mode 0A: 1 PLAYER / 2 PLAYER; $009E17 resets lives, powerups and score for a new game and goes to game mode $0B.

s009E6A.name: Table: menu entry counts
summary: Number of entries for each menu type (index = Y passed to the cursor routine): 2, 4, 2, 2, 4.

s009E74.name: Table: menu cursor VRAM addresses
summary: VRAM address (BG3 tilemap) of the first cursor tile of each menu type; the following entries are $40 (one tile row) apart.

s009E82.name: Draw blinking menu cursor
summary: Writes one stripe record per menu entry (cursor tile $2E or blank). The cursor blinks using [$1B91]; position is [$1B92].
Parameters: Y: menu type (0, 2, 4, 6, 8).

TBL_009EE0.name: Table: new game save data entries
summary: Pairs of (offset into the save data, value) written by CODE_WRITEOW: offset $28 = 3, $4D = 1, $52 = 1, $53 = 1, $5B = 8, $5C = 2,
$57 = 4, $30 = 1. The first offset is at TBL_009EE0 and the first value at DATA_009EE1.

TBL_009EF0.name: Table: new game overworld state
summary: 22 initial bytes written to the save data copy of $1F11-$1F26 (Mario and Luigi submap, positions, etc).

CODE_WRITEOW.name: Initialize new save file data
summary: Clears the working save data $1F49-$1FD5 and writes the defaults from TBL_009EE0 and TBL_009EF0.

KeepModeActive.name: Set fade step delay
summary: Sets the fade delay counter [$0DB1] to 1. $009F2B sets it to A.

s009F2F.name: Table: fade step values
summary: Indexed by fade direction ([$0DAF]). $009F2F: brightness step (+1, -1). $009F31: mosaic size step (-$10, +$10).
$009F33: brightness that ends the fade ($0F, $00); two further entries ($00, $F0) look unused.

TmpFade.name: Game modes 0F/13: fade with mosaic
summary: Fades brightness [$0DAE] and mosaic size [$0DB0] by one step every other frame. When the final brightness is reached the game
mode is incremented and the direction [$0DAF] is flipped. Mosaic is applied to BG1 and BG2.

GM++Mosaic.name: Advance game mode, apply mosaic; fade
summary: $009F5B: game mode++, flip the fade direction, set MOSAIC. $009F6F: fade step without mosaic (brightness only) used by many game
modes. $009F7C: slower fade (delay 8) used for the ending fade.

s009F88.name: Table: layer 3 setup per tileset
summary: 16 tilesets x 3 bytes (layer 3 type 1-3). Positive: effect value for [$1403]. $80: copy palette, $81: image with BG3 scroll, $C0: none.

s009FB8.name: Set up layer 3 (BG3) for the level
summary: Looks up the layer 3 setup in DATA_009F88 for tileset [$1931] and type [$1BE3], sets BG3 scroll, color math and uploads the
layer 3 image through Layer3Ptr. Called when a level is loaded.

in1Remember.name: Layer 3 setup, continued; clear L3 RAM
summary: $00A001-$00A044: second half of the layer 3 setup (palette copy for type $80, BG3 scroll, image upload).
$00A045: clears $B0 bytes of every $100-byte block of $7E:E400-$7E:FAFF and sets bit 7 of [RAM_IsVerticalLvl].

s00A06B.name: Table: overworld X start per submap
summary: Layer 1 X position for each overworld submap 0-6, indexed by submap * 2.

s00A079.name: Table: overworld Y start per submap
summary: Layer 1 Y position for each overworld submap 0-6, indexed by submap * 2.

LoadMapGameMode.name: Game mode 0C: load overworld
summary: Loads the overworld. If [$0109] is non-zero the map is skipped and the game goes straight to Mario Start (game mode $10).
Otherwise it uploads graphics and palettes, saves the player's lives, powerup, coins, Yoshi and reserve item, handles the game over
case (reload saved data, CONTINUE/END or title screen), and positions the map for the current player's submap.

ConfMapFromSave.name: Copy save data to overworld state
summary: Copies $8D bytes from $1F49-$1FD5 (save data in RAM) to $1EA2-$1F2E (live overworld data).

Clear_1A_13D3.name: Clear RAM; game mode 0E: overworld
summary: $00A1A6: clears [$1A]-[$D7] and $13D3-$1BA1.
$00A1BE: game mode 0E: runs the overworld each frame (SetUp0DA0GM4, hides sprites, GameMode_0E_Prim in bank $04, packs OAM size bits).

GrndShakeDispYHi.name: Table: ground shake Y offset (high); unknown
summary: $00A1D2: high bytes of the ground shake offsets. $00A1D6: unknown 4 byte table ($12, $22, $12, $02).
